subject: BYOK/KMS + SSO: handshake playbook and short-term evidence obligations
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Larsen <sara.larsen@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: BYOK/KMS + SSO: handshake playbook and short-term evidence obligations

Team —

Quick sync request: NovaMed has an upcoming security review week of Oct 19 and they want a clear "handshake" playbook for our BYOK/KMS + SSO integration that covers: evidence they can request, how we hand off audit logs, and an acceptable short-term retention carveout while we ship the longer-term retention control.

I sketched an obligation matrix (attached) that maps NovaMed asks -> our owner -> deliverable -> SLA. Can you each confirm the owner lines below and highlight any blockers we should resolve this week?

- Audit log access for user events (SSO auth, token issuance): Grace (traceability + sample export)
- Key custody evidence (KMS customer-managed key creation + rotation): Marissa (ops runbook + screenshots)
- Short-term retention exception (30-day ephemeral window for this pilot): Ben (decision record + legal sign-off)
- Rollout communications & support runbook: Kimberly/Jordan (customer-facing doc + escalation path)

Concrete asks:
1) Grace — can you confirm what exports we can provide by Oct 12 (schema + sample entries)?
2) Marissa — can you produce an ops artifact showing key lifecycle timestamps (creation, rotation) and access logs by Oct 14?
3) Ben — please coordinate legal template and a signed exception decision (we may need a DocuSign toy sheet) — target Oct 16.

I'll drop the obligation_matrix_v1.xlsx and a flow diagram (sso_kms_flow_v2.png) in Drive; adding HS-87932 to track.

Thanks — short thread please, we need to hand a compact packet to NovaMed security.

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Larsen <sara.larsen@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK/KMS + SSO: handshake playbook and short-term evidence obligations

Kimberly —

Thanks, noted. Quick answers from infra/observability side:
- We can provide an exported CSV of authentication events (SSO login, token issue, token refresh) with ISO timestamps and subject identifiers. Sample will be ready by Oct 12.
- Export will include fields: event_timestamp, user_id, auth_method, action, request_id, node_id. It will not include PII beyond user_id (internal GUID). If NovaMed needs email addresses we should gate that with legal.
- For real-time troubleshooting we can also deliver a 7-day live tail with correlation IDs, but that's higher friction (requires SOC approval).

Blockers:
- We need to confirm whether NovaMed requires user email in audit export (legal question).
- For the 30-day short-term retention exception, we need a clear purge mechanism scheduled after 30 days — I can add the purge job spec to the matrix.

I'll attach a sample CSV (reference link in Drive) and update the obligation matrix with the export schema.

Grace
Lead Security Engineer
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Larsen <sara.larsen@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK/KMS + SSO: handshake playbook and short-term evidence obligations

Morning —

I reviewed the KMS access paths. Concretely:
- We can produce a key lifecycle artifact that shows: key_create_time, key_version, rotation_events (timestamp + operator_id), and envelope-decryption-attempts (audit entries). I'll prepare a runbook snippet with screenshots of the customer-managed key console and CLI commands by Oct 14 as requested.
- Note: the KMS provider (customer-managed HSM) redacts raw key material — we can only show usage and metadata. That limitation should be explicit in the matrix.

Blockers for Marissa's deliverables:
1) Need clarity whether NovaMed requires per-operation principal IDs (e.g., which service account performed rotation) or if aggregated operator logs are acceptable.
2) If NovaMed requests signed attestations for rotation, we'll need legal input on signature format.

I'll update the obligation_matrix_v1.xlsx to include these caveats and a single-page ops runbook.

- Marissa
Director, Infrastructure Security
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Larsen <sara.larsen@novamed.com>, Legal - Acme Integrations <legal@acme-integrations.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK/KMS + SSO: handshake playbook and short-term evidence obligations

Copy — I'll own the exception decision coordination. To be explicit on next steps:
- I'll draft a "temporary exception decision record" that covers scope (NovaMed pilot only), duration (30 days), mitigations (audit export + retention purge), and acceptance criteria.
- Will route to Legal (cc'd) and our Compliance SME for sign-off. Target: draft ready Oct 9, sign-off Oct 16.

One policy question for Legal: does a 30-day ephemeral window require us to maintain a separate sealed evidence archive for the same 30 days in case of an audit request? If yes, we need to size storage and inform the sales contract.

Ben
Head of Sales Ops (contracts & entitlements)
From: Sara Larsen <sara.larsen@novamed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK/KMS + SSO: handshake playbook and short-term evidence obligations

Thanks all — this is very helpful. A couple clarifications from NovaMed's side:
- We don't need PII in the exports for the pilot; GUIDs are fine for now.
- We do want a signed decision record that explicitly says the 30-day ephemeral retention is an operational exception tied to the pilot and not a permanent SLA change. DocuSign is fine.
- For the sealed evidence archive: we can accept a time-boxed sealed archive (30 days) if Redwood can provide an index and a tamper-evidence hash for the archive. If that's heavy, we can accept operator-signed rotation logs instead.

If you can get the draft decision record into DocuSign by Oct 12, we can route internally and complete sign-off prior to the security review.

Best,
Sara Larsen
Head of Security Operations
NovaMed Health
